gap: No result ChatGPT got states that when the Sony WH-1000XM6 runs on its supplied cable, its Bluetooth is turned off and Sony tells you to answer calls on the phone and speak into the phone's microphone, so the headset's own mics only work for calls over Bluetooth. Among the over-ears compared, only the Jabra Evolve2 85 gives a laptop a separate path for calls: a Jabra Link USB Bluetooth adapter, sold in USB-A or USB-C and in Microsoft Teams or UC versions.
standout_why: The cited SoundGuys work page (soundguys.com/best-noise-cancelling-headphones-for-work-76177, read 2026-11-14) gives the Sony only a 'No USB listening' con. It says nothing about the Sony's mic going unused on the 3.5 mm cable. It covers the Teams vs Zoom/Meet versions and the USB-C adapter only for the Jabra Evolve3 85, not the Evolve2 85, and it does not cover the soundcore Space 2 Pro's lack of USB-C audio. The other cited page, the RTINGS phone-calls list, returned only navigation when I opened it, so I could not check its text. The SoundGuys honorable mention says the mic works over USB-C on the Bose QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), which is not the Ultra.
decides: This settles the pick for a shopper who calls from a PC. The Sony WH-1000XM6 and the soundcore Space 2 Pro can only carry laptop calls over Bluetooth Hands-Free (Sony says to pick 'Headset (WH-1000XM6 Hands-Free)' and warns that the Stereo/A2DP choice may make a video call unavailable). The Jabra Evolve2 85 adds a dedicated USB adapter, and its MS version is Teams-certified. So the Jabra is the pick for PC and Teams calls, and the Sony and soundcore suit a phone plus a laptop over Bluetooth.

findings.label: Mic and calls on the supplied headphone cable
findings.value: Bluetooth cannot be used while the cable is connected. For an incoming call the ring tone plays in the headset, and you answer on the smartphone and speak into the phone's microphone.
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Using the supplied headphone cable
findings.note: Sony's own Hints and Notes, paraphrased. The same page also says to turn off Speak-to-Chat before taking a call on the cable, or you won't hear the caller.

findings.label: Video calls on a computer: required profile
findings.value: Choose 'Headset (WH-1000XM6 Hands-Free)' (HFP/HSP) for both speaker and microphone. Sony warns that choosing music playback (A2DP, 'Headphones (WH-1000XM6 Stereo)') may make a video call unavailable.
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Making a video call on your computer
findings.note: The page says the connection is over Bluetooth and mentions no USB or wired option for calls. It also says: 'Depending on the video calling application you are using, this function may not be available.'

findings.label: Multipoint call handling
findings.value: 2 devices at once, turned on in the Sony | Sound Connect app. If a second call arrives during a first, you can answer it from the headset, but you cannot end the first call from the headset.
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Connecting the headset to 2 devices simultaneously (multipoint connection)
findings.note: Sony: 'If the second call is received without finishing the first call, the first call will continue silently.'

findings.label: LE Audio limits
findings.value: Uses the LC3 codec. Both the Android phone and the headset must support LE Audio. 'Some of the headset functions cannot be used' over LE Audio, and Sony says the connection prioritizes low latency at the cost of stability (reconnect with Classic Audio if it stutters).
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide: Pairing and connecting with an Android smartphone using LE Audio
findings.note: This page does not name which functions are lost.

findings.label: PC adapter and platform versions
findings.value: Comes in a Microsoft Teams-certified version and a UC version (Google Meet certified, 'optimized for other leading UC platforms'). The Bluetooth adapter can be USB-A or USB-C (Link 380a / Link 380c, each in UC and MS versions). Up to 2 simultaneous Bluetooth connections and up to 8 paired devices.
findings.note: Jabra's own page disagrees with itself about the adapter in the box: the tech-spec box list says 'Jabra Link 390 BT adapter' and the FAQ says 'Jabra Link 380'. Zoom certification is not listed on this page. The box list also includes a 1.2 m 3.5 mm jack audio cable and a USB-C to USB-A cable.

findings.label: Microphones
findings.note: Taken from the tech specs. Talk time is up to 26 h with ANC and busylight off, and up to 21 h with them on.

findings.label: Wired and USB-C audio
findings.value: Bluetooth and wired AUX only. Soundcore says it does 'not support audio transmission through the USB-C port.' Multipoint works in LDAC mode, but iOS devices do not support LDAC, and LDAC and Spatial Audio can't be on together.
findings.source_title: How can I get the best listening experience with Anker soundcore Space 2 Pro? | soundcore support
findings.note: The article does not say whether the headset mic works on the AUX cable.

findings.label: Wired connections
findings.value: USB-C audio at 16-bit, 44.1 or 48 kHz, plus a 3.5 mm to 2.5 mm audio cable in the box. Bluetooth 5.4 with profiles A2DP, HFP, AVRCP and BLE. $449.00 list (Cherry Chocolate).
findings.source_title: Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) | Bose
findings.note: The product page presents USB-C as a way to listen and does not say the microphone works over USB-C or the analog cable.

findings.label: Mic over USB-C (SoundGuys)
findings.value: SoundGuys says that plugging in over USB-C 'lets you listen and use the mic for calls over a single cable'.
findings.source_title: The best noise canceling headphones for work 2026: Tested and compared - SoundGuys
findings.note: This is the non-Ultra QuietComfort Headphones (2nd Gen), not the QC Ultra 2nd Gen on our page. The cited rival already has it.
